questions.prompt: Which statement is the law of conservation of energy?
options: Energy is used up when work is done
Energy can only be stored as heat
Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed
questions.explain: The total energy of an isolated system is constant.

questions.prompt: A 2 kg stone falls from 20 m. Ignoring air resistance, what is its kinetic energy just before it lands? (g = 9.8 N/kg)
questions.explain: KE gained = PE lost = mgh = 2 × 9.8 × 20 = 392 J.

questions.prompt: A ball is dropped from 5 m. How fast is it moving just before it hits the ground? (g = 10 N/kg, no air resistance)
A skater with no friction starts at 3 m on a half-pipe. How high does she reach on the other side?
questions.explain: With no friction, all the kinetic energy turns back into potential energy, so she reaches the same height.

questions.prompt: A bouncing ball rises lower after each bounce. Where does the missing energy go?
options: It goes into the ball’s mass
It is transferred to heat and sound
questions.explain: Energy is dissipated to the surroundings; it is not destroyed.

questions.prompt: Put the energy changes in a hydroelectric power station in order.
steps: Water stored high in a dam (gravitational potential energy)
Water turns the turbine (kinetic energy of the turbine)
questions.explain: Energy is transformed step by step; some is dissipated as heat and sound at each stage.

questions.prompt: Two balls of 1 kg and 4 kg are dropped from the same height with no air resistance. Which lands faster?
options: The 4 kg ball, twice as fast
They land at the same speed
questions.explain: mgh = ½mv²: the mass cancels, so v = √(2gh) for both.

questions.prompt: A 0.1 kg ball is dropped from 2 m and bounces back to 1.5 m. How much energy was dissipated? (g = 10 N/kg)
questions.explain: PE at 2 m = 0.1 × 10 × 2 = 2 J; at 1.5 m = 1.5 J; dissipated = 0.5 J.
